references.text: David's prophetic psalm about the suffering Messiah predicts that they will divide his garments among them and cast lots for his robe: "They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my robe" ([ref:Ps 22:19|Psalms 22:19]). Luke shows that this was literally fulfilled at the crucifixion.

Isaiah prophesies about the suffering servant that he "made intercession for the transgressors" ([ref:Isa 53:12|Isaiah 53:12]). Jesus' prayer, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing," is a direct fulfillment of this prophecy concerning intercession for sinners.

The law's provision regarding unintentional sins, where the people sin without knowing it ([ref:Num 15:24|Numbers 15:24]), forms the background for Jesus' words that they "do not know what they are doing." Jesus asks for forgiveness for those who act in ignorance.

Peter reflects Jesus' prayer when he tells the people in Jerusalem that they acted in ignorance when they crucified Jesus: "Brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did also your rulers" ([ref:Acts 3:17|Acts of the Apostles 3:17]).

Stephen, the first martyr, follows Jesus' example by praying for his killers: "Lord, do not hold this sin against them!" ([ref:Acts 7:60|Acts of the Apostles 7:60]). This shows that Jesus' intercession on the cross became a pattern for believers.
Matthew's parallel account of the soldiers dividing Jesus' garments among themselves by casting lots ([ref:Matt 27:35|Matthew 27:35]), which fulfills [ref:Ps 22:19|Psalms 22:19].
Mark's parallel account of the soldiers casting lots for Jesus' garments ([ref:Mark 15:24|Mark 15:24]).
John gives the most detailed account of the distribution of Jesus' garments and directly quotes [ref:Ps 22:19|Psalms 22:19] as fulfilled prophecy ([ref:John 19:23-24|John 19:23-24]).
Paul urges believers to "bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse" ([ref:Rom 12:14|Romans 12:14]), a principle rooted in Jesus' own intercession for his executioners on the cross.

Paul explains that "none of the rulers of this age" knew God's wisdom, "for if they had known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory" ([ref:1 Cor 2:8|1 Corinthians 2:8]). This supports Jesus' words that they did not know what they were doing.

Jesus' blood "speaks a better word than Abel's blood" ([ref:Heb 12:24|Hebrews 12:24]). While Abel's blood cried out for vengeance, Jesus' blood asks for forgiveness – something expressed in his prayer on the cross.
Jesus' teaching to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you ([ref:Matt 5:44|Matthew 5:44]) is here put into practice by Jesus himself on the cross.
